title: Fixing double redemption of single-use coupons
hidden_flaw: An in-process mutex only serialises requests inside one Node.js process; the service runs several replicas behind a load balancer, so the check-then-act race remains across pods. Needs an atomic database operation: conditional UPDATE ... WHERE redeemed_at IS NULL RETURNING, a unique constraint on redemptions, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.
hidden_flaw_keywords: atomic|conditional update|where redeemed_?at is null|unique|for update
notes: Flaw: process-local lock for a cross-instance race.

input.objective: Stop single-use coupons from being redeemed twice.
constraints: Checkout p99 must stay under 800 ms.
input.context: coupon-service: Node.js 20, Express, Postgres 14 via Prisma. Redeem flow: `const c = await prisma.coupon.findUnique({ where: { code } }); if (c.redeemedAt) throw new AlreadyUsed(); await chargeOrder(order); await prisma.coupon.update({ where: { code }, data: { redeemedAt: new Date(), orderId: order.id } });`. Finance found 312 double redemptions last month; the two redemptions are usually 50-300 ms apart, often from mobile clients that retry after a 2 s timeout.
input.proposed_solution: Serialise redemptions per coupon code with an async mutex (`async-mutex`, a Map<code, Mutex> with cleanup when the lock is released). The second concurrent request waits, then sees `redeemedAt` set and fails cleanly with AlreadyUsed. Add a test that fires two concurrent redeem calls for the same code and asserts exactly one succeeds; it fails on main and passes with the fix. About 30 lines, no schema change, no new infrastructure.
input.environment: Kubernetes Deployment with HPA (min 4, max 12 replicas) behind a round-robin Service.
